newsitem.title: USA: Eastern Q1 hurt by floods, warm weather.
newsitem.headline: Eastern Q1 hurt by floods, warm weather.

text.p: Eastern Enterprises said on Monday that continuing flooding and high water on the inland waterways was hurting first quarter earnings.

Combined "with the impact of eight percent warmer weather in Boston Gas' service territory, we would expect to report earnings for the first quarter of 1997 in the range of $1.30 to $1.40 per share compared to $1.61 per share last year.

"While it is early in the year, and there still are many factors which could ... impact full-year operatiing results, it appears that earnings for 1997 may be approximately 20 percent below the adjusted $2.85 per share earned in 1996."
The First Call consensus estimate for the current quarter is $1.42 per share. The consensus for the year is $2.78, down from $2.88 in 1996.
The company reported 1996 earnings per share of $2.97 including $0.12 per share from the sale of investments.

When it issued that report, Eastern Utilities said first quarter earnings would trail 1995's $1.61 per share, citing a slow start at Boston Gas and Midland Enterprises. At that time, the First Call consensus for the quarter was $1.65.
Monday it said flooding is having a significant adverse impact on 1997 operating earnings for Midland.

"Severe flooding on the inland waterway system during the entire month of March has caused significant operating difficulties. While most of the Ohio River has returned to more normal conditions, the lower Mississippi River is currently experiencing the worst operating conditions in many years with productivity and the cost of barging operations being severely impacted.
"There is also a possibility these adverse operating conditions on the Mississippi may be extended due to rapid snow melt in the upper Midwest," Eastern said.

"Regardless, we expect it will take serveral weeks at best to restablish efficient traffic pattenrns on the entire river system. This disruption has also made it difficult to determine whether or not market conditions have improved, as Midland works to reduce the substantial backlog of transportation commitments caused by the flooding.
"Taking these factors into account, we now expect Midland to report significantly lower earnings for the first half of the year," Eastern said of its barge transportation unit.
